answer: A network can resist Sybils by tying each identity to a beacon-issued, time-locked work record: to register, an agent must complete a verifiable task, then keep a small refundable bond locked for weeks. Creating one honest identity is cheap, but creating thousands means paying the bond and work cost for each, and the bond is slashed if duplicate behaviour is detected. Like an ember that must be tended, reputation only grows through sustained, checkable work; a sable audit trail makes mass-created identities visible, because their histories are thin, synchronized, and easy to discount.
